text:
incident-bot: P0 - Multi-region failover triggered: automatic reroute us-west-2 -> ap-southeast-2 after provider reported AZ fabric errors. Post-failover: elevated 5xx, TLS fragmentation errors, and model-variant divergence observed. Incident ID 2034567890.

jordan (oncall): I'm taking this. Seeing spikes in 5xx and connection errors immediately after failover. Triage: routing/BGP, CDN anycast, IPv6 path MTU, LB healthchecks, autoscale.

priya (netops): Provider notice: partial inter-AZ packet loss in us-west-2 at ~2034567700. BGP updates triggered our failover at 2034567745. After reroute, I'm seeing asymmetric return paths for some IPv6 prefixes and signs of PMTU blackhole on certain transit hops. Packets > 1200 bytes get dropped in one path.

nate (eng-sre): App-level symptoms: clients report TLS handshake or early data failures, sometimes `tls: record overflow` or `TLS fragmentation error`. Edge logs show many client Hello packets but server never gets complete handshake due to fragmentation. Example log: 

```
[2034567801] edge-11: tls_handshake fail client=2401:db00::1 -> RST after 95ms (fragment-missing)
[2034567810] frontend-ap-02: healthcheck 200 ok but subsequent handshake fails
```

alina (platform): Observability: After the failover, our CDN anycast points continued to route some user traffic to legacy frontends in us-west-2 for ~40s due to stale origin maps. Those edges then attempted to connect to promoted ap-southeast-2 frontends over the IPv6 path exhibiting PMTU issues, producing many TLS failures. Also, autoscaling promoted a new worker AMI in ap-southeast-2 which hadn't yet loaded the v3.1 model, so a subset of requests returned older outputs.

auto-failover-bot: Automated action: region-failover us-west-2 -> ap-southeast-2 (act id AF-2034-7); auto-promote standby AMIs in ap-southeast-2 (act id AF-2034-8); reweight CDN origins (cdna-2034-2).

jordan (oncall): Immediate mitigations: 1) Cancel auto-promote until AMI parity verified. 2) Pause failover policy to stop further oscillation. 3) Force CDN origin revalidation and set affected POPs to prefer IPv4. 4) Apply PMTU workaround (force MSS clamping) on our transit where possible. 5) Switch LB healthcheck to TCP for frontends to avoid false positives from HTTP-only probes.

priya (netops): Executing commands now. Cancel auto-promote: `redwoodctl region promote cancel --action AF-2034-8` -> `OK - cancel queued (op-id cancel-203456-1)`. Pause failover: `redwoodctl failover pause --policy multi-region-auto --reason "provider flapping - manual hold"` -> `OK (op-id fop-2034-1)`.

alina (platform): Forcing CDN origin revalidation and IPv4 preference: `cdnctl revalidate-pops --pop-list 5 --prefer ipv4` -> returned `accepted`. Also setting origin TTL to 300s to reduce churn.

priya (netops): On the PMTU front, I can apply MSS clamping on our transit routers to 1200 bytes for affected egress prefixes. Doing that now with the provider ticket open (prov-ticket PT-2034-9).

nate (eng-sre): Also recommending we stop draining us-west-2 instances (if any) so long-lived sessions aren't killed mid-handshake. Cancel drain if active. `redwoodctl mitigation cancel --id DR-2034-5` -> `No active drain with id` (ok). But good to note we won't drain.

alina (platform): Switching LB healthchecks to TCP on ap-southeast-2 target groups: `aws elbv2 modify-target-group --target-group-arn arn:aws:... --health-check-protocol TCP --health-check-port 443` -> `success`. Health states re-evaluating. TCP probes avoid relying on app-level header that may be affected by partial handshake.

jordan (oncall): Customer-impact snapshot: endpoints /v1/generate and /v1/realtime had elevated TLS failures and 502/504s for ~15 minutes (2034567745 - 2034568630), affecting ~18% of requests in AP and some EU clients routed via certain Anycast POPs. Model-variant mismatch affected ~7% of requests due to AMI parity lag. Eric, can you start drafting a customer note?

eric (customer-success): On it. I'll ping top affected accounts and draft an incident update with timeline and mitigations.

nate (eng-sre): Observability update: after MSS clamping and forcing IPv4, TLS handshake failures dropped by ~65% within 90s. However some clients still hit legacy frontends due to CDN caches holding stale origin map. I'm purging origin map caches in those POPs now. `cdnctl purge-origins --pop 12,14` -> `purge queued`.

priya (netops): Provider update: they've applied a workaround on their side for the PMTU blackhole and confirmed that certain IX hops were dropping IPv6 fragments. They're coordinating a permanent fix. Ticket PT-2034-9 -> `status: workaround applied, monitoring`.

alina (platform): Regarding model parity: we canceled auto-promote but a few standby AMIs were already launched; I'm running a rapid job to pull v3.1 docker artifact and warm the model on those instances. `deployctl exec --region ap-southeast-2 --task warm-model --image redwood/model:v3.1` -> `warm tasks started on 4/4 nodes`.

jordan (oncall): Good. Additional follow-ups: 1) Add IPv6 PMTU/fragmentation monitors to our network health dashboards (owner: priya). 2) Add CDN origin map TTL safeguards to avoid stale mapping during failover (owner: alina). 3) Gate auto-promotion on AMI artifact parity (owner: alina + nate). 4) Add a runbook step: prefer IPv4 for inter-region control traffic during failover windows (owner: priya).

eric (customer-success): Draft customer note summarizing: cause: provider AZ fabric + IPv6 PMTU blackhole leading to TLS fragmentation; impact: elevated TLS failures and model divergence; mitigations: MSS clamping + IPv4 preference + cancelled auto-promote + model warmers + CDN revalidation; status: stabilized and monitoring. Sending to ops/comms for review.

nate (eng-sre): Quick log snippet showing improvement: 
```
[2034567992] edge-02: tls_handshake success client=203.15.6.9 via ipv4
[2034568005] frontend-ap-01: model warm v3.1 loaded - ready
```

priya (netops): Provider reports BGP stability improving and IPv6 fragment drops down to baseline. We've left MSS clamp in place for 2 hours per runbook to avoid recurrence.

alina (platform): CDN purges completed and origin maps now consistent. Model warmers finished; parity confirmed. I've added a pre-promotion check in the promo pipeline to ensure docker artifact digest matches canonical digest. PR opened: `platform/ci#412`.

jordan (oncall): On-call handoff: I'll stay for 30 more minutes then hand to nate. Leaving runbook notes and packet captures in PagerDuty. Anyone else need the handoff?

eric (customer-success): I'll monitor customer responses and update the incident page.

auto-failover-bot: Incident 2034567890 -> state: mitigated; monitoring. Contributors: jordan (oncall), priya (netops), nate (eng-sre), alina (platform), eric (customer-success).

jordan (oncall): Final quick timeline for postmortem: ~2034567700 provider AZ fabric errors; ~2034567745 auto-failover to ap-southeast-2; ~2034567760 CDN stale origin mapping + IPv6 PMTU blackhole observed; ~2034567785 auto-promote launched; ~2034567805 MSS clamp + IPv4 preference applied + cancel auto-promote; ~2034567850 TLS failures drop after purges and clamping; ~2034567920 model warmers finish; ~2034568123 monitoring.

priya (netops): I'll own the PMTU monitoring dashboard and the runbook step to prefer IPv4 during provider flapping.

alina (platform): I'll own the promo-gate PR and CDN origin TTL safeguards.

nate (eng-sre): I'll own the postmortem doc (inc-2034567890) and the AMI parity checks.

eric (customer-success): I'll finish and send the customer comms.

incident-bot: Incident 2034567890 status set to MONITORING by jordan (oncall).
